title: Strategic Shores: Strengthening Overseas Port Infrastructure to Safeguard U.S. Economic and Security Interests
summary_en: Global seaports have become a key arena for U.S.-China strategic competition. A new CSIS report examines vulnerabilities across the maritime port sector and offers recommendations to strengthen U.S. competitiveness and security overseas.
title_cn: Strategic Shores: Strengthening Overseas Port Infrastructure to Safeguard U.S. Economic and Security Interests

title: Strategic Shores: Strengthening Overseas Port Infrastructure to Safeguard U.S. Economic and Security Interests (Country Case Studies)
summary_en: Global seaports have become an important arena for strategic competition, creating new economic and security challenges for the United States. Drawing on field visits and interviews, four CSIS case studies examine port infrastructure in Panama, Peru, Sri Lanka, and Greece.
title_cn: Strategic Shores: Strengthening Overseas Port Infrastructure to Safeguard U.S. Economic and Security Interests (Country Case Studies)

title: One Year After Busan: Has China Kept Its Rare Earth Promises?
summary_en: One year after Busan, China’s rare earth exports to the United States remain sharply below pre-restriction levels, even as global shipments hold steady. Beijing’s continued control over rare earth supplies raises the stakes for Trump-Xi meetings in Shenzhen and Miami.
title_cn: One Year After Busan: Has China Kept Its Rare Earth Promises?
